original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-point-functor}
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a functor. Let
$v : \mathcal{D} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor and set
$w = v \circ u$. Denote $q$, resp., $p$ the stalk functor
(\ref{equation-stalk}) associated to $v$, resp.\ $w$.
Then $(u_p\mathcal{F})_q = \mathcal{F}_p$ functorially in the
presheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.
review_scope: pinned original Stacks theorem and relevant site-point definitions; proofs not reviewed
hold_reason: Both the hypothesis and statement use the raw '(\ref{equation-stalk})' instead of specifying the p- and q-stalk functors for w=v∘u and v. The comparison (u_pF)_q=F_p requires that missing standalone construction.
proposed_correction: Define both stalk constructions using the respective neighbourhood categories of v and w=v∘u, remove raw equation ref, keep the u_p adjunction and functorial identification, independently re-review.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-point-morphism-sites}
\begin{slogan}
A map of sites defines a map on points, and pullback respects stalks.
\end{slogan}
Let $f : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a morphism of sites
given by a continuous functor $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$.
Let $q$ be a point of $\mathcal{D}$ given by the functor
$v : \mathcal{D} \to \textit{Sets}$, see
Definition \ref{definition-point}.
Then the functor $v \circ u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$
defines a point $p$ of $\mathcal{C}$ and moreover there is
a canonical identification
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal{F})_q = \mathcal{F}_p
$$
for any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.
review_scope: pinned original Stacks theorem and relevant site-point definitions; proofs not reviewed
hold_reason: The source's 'Definition \ref{definition-point}' reference remains inside the hypothesis of the point-pullback theorem, without independently stating that v:D→Sets satisfies the point axioms. The exact stalk compatibility is otherwise preserved.
proposed_correction: Specify that v represents a topos point satisfying the site-point coverage and finite-limit conditions, remove the raw Definition ref and retain both point-composition and stalk-identification clauses, independently re-review.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-point-morphism-topoi}
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$
be a morphism of topoi. Let $q : \Sh(pt) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$
be a point. Then $p = f \circ q$ is a point of the topos
$\Sh(\mathcal{C})$ and we have
a canonical identification
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal{F})_q = \mathcal{F}_p
$$
for any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.
